questions.question: Write a SQL query to find duplicate users
questions.context: Mid-level DS interview at fintech company

follow_ups.text: What if you needed to find users who created duplicate accounts across different time periods?
How would you optimize this for a table with 100M rows?
Should you use GROUP BY or DISTINCT? When would each fail?
follow_ups.intent: test SQL fundamentals and edge cases

questions.key_insight: Duplicate detection isn't just a GROUP BY—it's about understanding what constitutes a duplicate in your business context

questions.question: Build a churn prediction model—walk me through your approach
questions.context: Standard DS interview across fintech, B2B SaaS, e-commerce

follow_ups.text: Why would you choose XGBoost over logistic regression here?
follow_ups.intent: test understanding of model selection tradeoffs

follow_ups.text: Your model gets 95% accuracy. Is that good? Why or why not?
follow_ups.intent: test business acumen and class imbalance awareness

follow_ups.text: You achieved 92% accuracy but 50% false positive rate. How do you decide if this is production-ready?
follow_ups.intent: test production thinking and stakeholder communication

questions.key_insight: Senior engineers choose models based on business constraints (FP cost, latency, maintainability), not accuracy alone

questions.question: How would you detect model drift in production?
questions.context: Production ML roles, companies with mature ML infrastructure

follow_ups.text: What's the difference between data drift and model drift?
You detect drift. What do you do next? Retrain? Rollback? How do you decide?
How would you automate this monitoring without creating alert fatigue?

questions.key_insight: Drift detection alone is useless—you need a decision framework for when to act and what action to take

questions.question: Explain Type I vs Type II error with a real example from your work

follow_ups.text: In your example, which error is more expensive to your business?
follow_ups.intent: test tradeoff thinking and business impact awareness

follow_ups.text: How would you design your test to minimize the costlier error?
You run the experiment for 7 days and get p=0.08. Do you stop or keep running?
follow_ups.intent: test understanding of p-hacking and when to stop

questions.key_insight: Statistical significance isn't a binary switch—it's a tool for decision-making, and you need to know what error costs you more

questions.question: Design a real-time recommendation system
questions.context: Senior DS interviews at scale-up / big tech

follow_ups.text: Walk me through your latency budget. Where do you spend it?
follow_ups.intent: test systems thinking and tradeoff awareness

follow_ups.text: Your model training takes 6 hours. How do you keep recommendations fresh without retraining constantly?
How would you A/B test this system without a madhouse of feature flags?

questions.key_insight: Real-time systems are about constraints—latency, freshness, cost—and making principled tradeoffs across them
